open: The 48055 signature on the card (atomId and atomDid differ, nodeId and claim hash equal) is unreachable from this tree for one landing row; the planner reads run_events for 1956886d leg=replay fieldDiff.fields to see whether it was the binding-order signature [atomId, nodeId, atomDid] or the tie-order signature [atomId, atomDid, claim]; both are fixed here either way.

Replay hydration now excludes rows stamped at this run's knowledgeAt so fixture (b) can fire; the card's literal (a) wording had pass two reading pass one's rows, under which a random mint is invisible to the check. Planner accepts or the filter comes out with (b) marked unable to fire.

Tier-1 binding is earliest-known first: counties with random-era alias sets (48055 four per key, Bastrop 3.18 per key by the card's arithmetic) keep binding to the earliest random-era node, not the deterministic one; a repoint to deterministic ids is a V9 decision outside this card.

Persisting the emitted alias set per chunk means one new era row per key per run; the aliases table keeps growing one set per run. Reusing the earliest era when the binding is unchanged would stop it; era semantics decision for the planner.

Migration 0004 must be applied (factory-conformant-migrate) before the loop or manifest-read runs on the new image; an unapplied column fails the f10_county_runs INSERT and the manifest degraded SELECT loud, never silently.

LESSON: A replay that hydrates what the first pass persisted is internal consistency: a random mint passed it. Cold replay must read the state the run started from (knowledge_at < run knowledgeAt).
atomId is a pure function of (nodeId, claim, logicVersion); a diff claiming atomId differs while both agree is a reading to re-verify, not a mechanism to hunt.
The card's staged-atom counts encode the hydrated alias count: 48055 783,710 = 4.0 prior sets per key; 48085 2,174,668 = 0 prior sets. Arithmetic on a symptom is a free instrument.
DEAD-END: Adding ORDER BY to loadAliasRows as the binding-order fix: it would be a second implementation of one rule next to the in-memory sort; the sort in resolveCandidate is the single control and the fake returns rows unordered on purpose.
Running the migration against the local PostgreSQL 18: refused under the no-database rule; CI's migrate step exercises it.
